item.title: The Message 1.4.0
item.description:
What's new

A notebook for your study

  • Write notes in the new Notebook (⌥⌘3). They're plain Markdown files in a folder you choose, so they open in Obsidian or any editor too.
  • Type [[ to link a sermon, a paragraph, a verse or another note. Links open right where they point.
  • Choose Add to Note… on a paragraph, a verse or a highlight to send it to a note with its link.
  • "In your notes" shows, beside a sermon or a chapter, every note that links to it.

The Study Center

  • Press ⌥⌘I in the Bible. It follows the verse you're reading, or the verses you select.
  • Commentaries: what Matthew Henry, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, John Gill, Adam Clarke, and Keil and Delitzsch say on the verse. Click one to read it beside the chapter. They're read online the first time, then kept on your Mac.
  • Hebrew and Greek: the words behind the KJV, and the verse word by word in the original with each word's parsing.
  • Easton's and Smith's Bible dictionaries and Nave's Topical Bible: the articles and topics that cite the verse. Select a name and choose Look Up to read about it.
  • Also cross references, the sermons that cite the verse, and when it happened on a timeline from Creation to Paul in Rome.

A Bible atlas

  • The places in a chapter appear on a map of the land as it was, with no modern towns or roads. A "?" marks a site scholars still debate.
  • Journeys are drawn in red, the way they went: Paul's journeys, the Exodus, Abram to Haran.
  • The layers button outlines regions and can shade the Persian Empire, Alexander's empire, Herod's kingdom, or the Roman Empire.
  • The atlas is built into the app and works offline.

And

  • Select words in either reader to search the Bible or the sermons for them.
  • Highlight categories can each take a colour of your own and a style: highlight, marker or underline.
  • Bibles in thirteen more languages can be downloaded in Settings → Translations: Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Serbian, Spanish, Swahili, Tagalog and Tamil.

item.title: The Message 1.3.0
item.description:
What's new

Six new looks for the stream, the projector and your videos

  • Vigil: black, big bold titles set to the left over a streak of blue light, with the date and your church along the foot.
  • Covenant: deep ultramarine with a scatter of stars, everything centred.
  • Psalter: cream paper, Didot and prayer-book red, like a printed page.
  • Monument: stone and signal orange, with one giant word or number behind the title: the countdown, the verse's chapter and number, or Amen.
  • Halftone: deep blue printed over with fine dots and a light serif.
  • Clean: words alone over a busy camera shot.

Make your own

  • Studio Look has new choices: a layout (centred, editorial or monument), one pattern for the background (paper grain, stars, halftone, a streak of light or a grid), and how the small words are set.
  • New typefaces: Didot, SF Pro Heavy and Avenir Next Condensed.
  • A look you saved before keeps working.

item.title: The Message 1.2.1
item.description:
What's new

Easier to install

  • The download is now a disk image: open it and drag The Message onto the Applications folder beside it.
  • If The Message is opened from Downloads or from the disk image, it explains how to move it into Applications, where it can update itself.

item.title: The Message 1.2.0
item.description:
What's new

Updates inside the app

  • The Message now updates itself. It looks for a new version once a day and shows what's new before installing it; choose The Message → Check for Updates… to look now.
  • Settings → Updates can turn the daily check off, or let updates download and install by themselves when you quit.
  • Updates are signed, so only real releases of The Message install.

This is the last version you need to download from the site: from here on, updates arrive in the app.
